clue.text: Bags left in bags

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the second set of bags

parts.note: bags are sacks

explanation.surface: Something left behind inside some carrier bags.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Bags' is the definition, an old informal word for trousers; the second gives SACKS, with L put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is a dated British word for loose trousers, the same garments as slacks.

clue.text: The French left a confused flier

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: confused means the letters of left are mixed up

explanation.surface: A French person leaves behind a bewildered pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a printed handout, the same as a leaflet.

clue.text: Share half of beer — that's cleverer

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings

indicators.note: half of takes the back two letters of beer

explanation.surface: Splitting a beer is the smarter move.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute can mean shrewd or clever, so cuter means cleverer.

clue.text: Loss of stock from years under psychiatrist?

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts one piece below the other

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: Losing one's stock after years of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the loss of retail stock through theft or damage.

clue.text: What are worn at work, generally before start of strike?

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: overall means generally, taken as a whole

indicators.note: start of asks for the opening letter of strike

explanation.surface: A question about what workers usually wear just before a walkout begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are protective garments pulled on over clothes for manual work.

clue.text: What copper may be when out of uniform?

definitions.text: What copper may be when out of uniform?

parts.words: What copper may be when out of uniform?
parts.note: a police officer off duty is not walking the rounds, while the word also means unconventional, out of the uniform way

explanation.surface: What a police officer is when off duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional, departing from the uniform norm.

clue.text: Wrinkled, lacking credit but comforted

indicators.note: lacking means a piece is taken away from the wrinkled word

parts.note: creased means wrinkled

explanation.surface: Wrinkled and without credit, yet consoled.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone is to relieve or soothe them.

clue.text: Lamenting changes in political allegiance

indicators.note: changes means the letters of lamenting are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone mourning a switch of party loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Alignment is a stance of support for a party or cause.

clue.text: Permit covers nine — dangerously lax

indicators.note: covers means one piece wraps around another

parts.note: to let is to permit

indicators.note: dangerously suggests the letters of nine are thrown about

explanation.surface: A permit covering nine people is dangerously slack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' looks like a noun for a licence, but it is the verb, and 'dangerously' scrambles the number that LET wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant or not strict, which is lax.

clue.text: Looking for a design, in a way

parts.note: to be after something is to be looking for it
a fashion is a design or style

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a pattern, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to some extent or not very well, much as in a way does.

clue.text: The girl who's left gold in the keeping of criminal buyer?

indicators.note: being in the keeping of something means being held inside it

parts.note: a fence buys and sells stolen goods
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A girl has left her gold with a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is a girl's name, so it can stand for some girl.

clue.text: Head of crime family needs essential drug-runner

parts.note: a don is the boss of a Mafia family
key means essential or crucial

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss needs a vital courier for his narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug courier is called a mule, and a mule is a beast of burden like a donkey.

clue.text: Bitter setback in South Africa's levels of society

indicators.note: in shows one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

indicators.note: setback means the word for bitter is put back to front

parts.note: tart means bitter or sour

explanation.surface: A bitter reverse in South Africa's social hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' reverses only the bitter word; South Africa's abbreviation then wraps round it, with 'Bitter' disguised as a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, used figuratively for social classes or levels.

clue.text: Genial Navy bunch — full bars with no outsiders

indicators.note: with no outsiders means each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A friendly group of sailors filling the bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Avuncular means kindly and friendly, like a good uncle.

clue.text: Carrier carrying item of underwear — it's a farce!

indicators.note: carrying means one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a tray is something used for carrying things
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone bringing in an undergarment on a tray, which is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is worn under a shirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque imitation, as a farce is.

clue.text: A job with a group on the rise for these renegades

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: on the rise in a down clue means a word is read upwards

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Turncoats who join a rising group for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostates are people who abandon their faith or party, which renegades do.

clue.text: Sort sure to crash in lower gear

indicators.note: to crash is to smash up, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of crash happening when in a low gear in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Trousers are clothing for the lower body, so they are gear worn down below.

clue.text: Dish that's unusual and something of a bore

parts.note: rare means unusual
a drill bit is what bores the hole

explanation.surface: A peculiar meal that is a little dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the drilling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, Welsh rarebit, is a cheese-on-toast dish.

clue.text: Areas where head of state is apprehensive, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means what follows is heard, a spoken likeness

parts.note: the opening letter of state, S, with fears for being apprehensive

explanation.surface: Regions where the leader of a country is nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, S plus FEARS sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres are areas of activity or influence.

clue.text: Reveal rent for retail store

parts.note: to out someone or something is to reveal it
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Disclosing the rent paid for a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a shop or point of sale for goods.

clue.text: Within context, remember the highest limit

indicators.note: within signals the letters lying inside these words

explanation.surface: Bearing in mind the upper limit within context.
explanation.definitionFit: An extreme is the furthest or highest point, a limit.

clue.text: Supports people in case of bias

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
case of means the outer letters of bias, its casing

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: Support groups for people in cases of prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Braces are supports, such as struts or the straps holding up trousers.

clue.text: Dress for work duty

explanation.definitionFit: A shift is both a loose dress and a spell of work duty.

clue.text: Running a temperature, shows sign of exhaustion wearing these

parts.note: running a temperature means feeling hot
someone exhausted pants for breath

explanation.surface: A hot, breathless person wearing skimpy shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these' points to the garments being worn by the overheated runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotpants are very short shorts, the garments the clue points to.

clue.text: A second letter is read out in church

indicators.note: is read out means the letters are spoken aloud

parts.note: A followed by B, the second letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter is read aloud in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying A then the letter B out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastery church.

clue.text: Blair? I'd bet all worried about game played here

indicators.note: worried about means the letters are tossed around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Tony Blair says he bet on everything, worrying about some game.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is the former British prime minister Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is played on a cloth-covered table, the place where that game happens.

clue.text: States repeatedly breaking treaties

indicators.note: breaking means the word treaties is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Nations repeatedly breaking treaties.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do something again and again.

clue.text: Manners covered in hasty lessons

indicators.note: covered in means the letters sit enclosed within these words

explanation.surface: Manners taught in a rushed class.
explanation.definitionFit: Styles are manners or ways of doing things.
